title: Explain Cloud Computing Service Models (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS)
summaryPoint: The three core functional layers of cloud service provisioning based on management responsibilities.
keyPoints: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service): Delivers virtualized computer hardware, storage disks, and networking infrastructure (e.g. Amazon EC2, Google Compute Engine).
PaaS (Platform as a Service): Supplies runtime environments, operating systems, and developer toolchains for deploying applications without server management (e.g. AWS Elastic Beanstalk).
SaaS (Software as a Service): Delivers end-user software applications hosted in the cloud and accessed through web browsers (e.g. Google Workspace, Microsoft 365).

title: Explain Cloud Deployment Models (Public, Private, Hybrid, Community)
summaryPoint: Defines where cloud infrastructure is located, access boundaries, and organizational ownership.
keyPoints: Public Cloud: Multi-tenant computing infrastructure owned by third-party providers accessible to the general public over the internet.
Private Cloud: Dedicated cloud infrastructure maintained exclusively for a single enterprise organization.
Hybrid Cloud: An integrated infrastructure bridging public and private clouds, enabling dynamic data portability.
Community Cloud: Cloud shared between organizations having common regulatory requirements, missions, or security protocols.

title: Explain Core Components of Internet of Things (IoT) Architecture
summaryPoint: Network of interconnected physical items exchanging sensor data across communication networks.
keyPoints: Sensors & Actuators: Sensors collect physical environmental variables (temperature, motion, light), while actuators carry out physical physical operations based on sensor triggers.
Connectivity: Communication pathways (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Zigbee, Cellular) routing sensory telemetry to centralized gateways.
Data Processing: Cloud analytics software transforming sensory telemetries into actionable monitoring insights.

title: Explain Key Advantages and Features of 5G Cellular Technology
summaryPoint: Fifth-generation telecommunication wireless standard bringing lower latency and greater bandwidth.
keyPoints: Ultra-High Throughput: Data transmission rates up to 10 to 20 Gbps, which is significantly faster than 4G LTE networks.
Ultra-Low Latency: Latency drops to under 1 millisecond, supporting real-time applications such as autonomous vehicles and remote surgery.
Massive Device Connectivity: Supports connecting millions of concurrent IoT devices per square kilometer without network congestion.
